title: Hard-Alloy Print Recipes via Sample-Efficient AI Campaigns
one_liner: Sell validated 3D-print parameter recipes and 40-build AI-guided optimization campaigns so ordinary mid-power metal printers can make alloys that normally need rare high-power machines.
customer: Metal additive-manufacturing job shops and small rocket, space and defense suppliers with 400-500 W class printers. University AM labs are a secondary buyer.
problem: GRCop-42, a copper-chromium-niobium rocket-engine alloy, is hard and costly to print. It typically needs high laser power, and about 90% of commercial printers cannot handle it. Every failed build wastes powder and machine time, and shops cannot afford months of trial and error.
solution: A recipe library of machine-specific, validated parameter sets and build reports, sold per alloy and per machine model. It comes with a paid 'campaign' service that uses Bayesian or active-learning search to find working settings in about 40 builds from a few failed starting points. Customer builds feed back into the shared library.
why_now: Washington State University's team used AI to search over 100 million candidate settings, started from 37 failed experiments, and found 6 successful settings in 40 experiments over 3 months, including a first successful print at a record-low 500 W. The work won an Innovative Deployed Application Award, and active-learning frameworks for science are appearing on arXiv (for example arXiv:2609.31197). The method is proven and unlicensed to shops.
revenue_model: Recipe licenses at roughly $5-30k per alloy-machine pair, campaign fees of roughly $20-60k, and an annual recipe-library subscription for shops.
non_obvious_insight: The product is not the alloy but the experiment budget. The WSU study says 90% of commercial printers cannot print GRCop-42 and that success required 'a very challenging case for AI' with rare successes, and the lead author says they are 'essentially democratizing the printing' of the alloy (https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/08/260827010504.htm). Selling failure-avoidance to shops that cannot afford 37 failed builds is a service business, not a materials business.
first_30_days: Contact the WSU authors and WSU's commercialization office about licensing the method. Recruit 2-3 job shops with 400-500 W machines and quote a fixed-price GRCop-42 campaign, with the shop supplying powder and machine time. Pre-sell the first recipe pack to rocket and space startups. Run the first campaign in month 2 and publish a build-report case study.

title: Rescue Monitoring for Orphaned Home Solar
one_liner: An installer-agnostic gateway plus subscription that watches home solar systems whose installer went bankrupt, produces warranty-ready evidence, and dispatches a vetted local electrician.
customer: Homeowners with installer-abandoned solar systems (owned or financed). B2B: solar loan servicers and asset managers holding loans and leases from failed installers, who care about collateral performance. Local electricians and solar technicians are the fulfillment network.
problem: Installers such as Sunnova (Chapter 11 in June 2025, roughly 500,000 customers) and others collapsed. Systems keep running, but nobody is watching or servicing them. Silent faults (failed optimizers, tripped rapid shutdown, inverter errors) can cost months of production. Warranty claims require documentation the homeowner doesn't have, and installer apps degrade or vanish.
solution: A gateway that reads inverter data locally (SunSpec Modbus and local APIs) plus a CT clamp on the main panel. It compares actual output to modeled output using open weather and irradiance data, classifies probable fault types (string, inverter, shading, curtailment), and generates a warranty evidence pack for the equipment manufacturers. A flat-fee price sheet dispatches vetted local technicians. Start with the three or four most common inverter families.
why_now: The installer failure wave (SunPower in 2024, Sunnova in 2025, many smaller firms) is producing large orphaned fleets. The federal residential solar tax credit ended for expenditures after 2025, so more installers will exit and fewer new ones will absorb the orphans. Gateways and cloud analytics are now cheap.
revenue_model: USD 8-12 per month plus a USD 150-250 gateway or a USD 199 'solar health check plus 12 months' bundle. Dispatch margin of 15-20% on repairs. B2B data-and-triage feed of USD 2-4 per system per month for servicers with 10k+ systems.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce thing isn't data, because the inverter clouds still exist. It's someone accountable who reads the data and moves a truck. Sell a primary-care doctor for a solar system with a referral network. Lenders care because a non-producing system correlates with default, which gives a second payer.
first_30_days: Recruit orphan-solar homeowners through r/solar and Facebook groups. Ship 50 gateways to owners of two or three inverter families. Sign 3-5 electricians in Texas, California, Arizona or Florida on a fixed price sheet. Sell the health-check bundle and use the first detected faults as marketing proof. Approach two loan servicers with the aggregate underperformance findings.

title: Passive Wellness Alerts From Water Meter Patterns
one_liner: A subscription that texts an adult child, or their parent's home-care agency, when an older person living alone has no expected water activity: no wearable, no camera, just the meter that is already on the house.
customer: Adult children of seniors who live alone ($12-19 per month). Home-care agencies and Area Agencies on Aging, which pay about $15-25 per client per month for a passive check on clients between visits. Later, Medicare Advantage plans offering supplemental benefits, at a per-member-per-month rate. Utilities are the channel partner, not the main payer.
problem: Roughly a quarter or more of Americans aged 65 and older live alone. Existing safety products get abandoned: pendants are left on the nightstand, wearables aren't charged, and cameras feel like surveillance and get unplugged. Families end up making anxious phone calls. Meanwhile the utility already has hour-level (or finer) consumption data from its smart meter, used only for bill disputes and leak alerts. Nobody has to wear or charge a meter.
solution: Learn each household's rhythm from interval water data: first use in the morning, number of daily events, typical overnight quiet. Alert on: no water event by the person's usual time plus a buffer, unusually long or repeated overnight use (possible wandering or confusion), continuous flow (leak or overflow), and sudden spikes. Escalate by text to a family member, then to a designated neighbor or a non-emergency wellness-check partner. Two data paths. Path A is a $40-bill-of-materials clamp-on or pulse reader on the customer's own meter, installed in 15 minutes by a caregiver, which needs no utility integration. Path B is a customer-consented feed from the utility's smart-meter system, with no hardware and utility co-branding. Leak protection is a free bonus that sells the same product to the utility.
why_now: The oldest baby boomers are now in their 80s, and 'Peak 65' has meant around 4 million Americans turning 65 every year through 2027. Home-care labor is scarce, so agencies need passive tools that extend a caregiver's reach. Smart-meter adoption among mid-size and large water utilities is now high, and those utilities are looking for customer-engagement wins after the billing complaints that followed rollouts. Green Button-style customer-directed data sharing exists for electricity but is almost absent for water. LLMs can also explain a pattern change in plain language to worried families.
revenue_model: Family subscription of $12-19 per month, plus optional hardware at cost or $49. B2B2C contracts with home-care agencies at $15-25 per client per month. Revenue share or flat fees from utilities per opted-in household. Later, Medicare Advantage supplemental-benefit contracts.
non_obvious_insight: Water use is the most honest sign of life in a house. Nobody can skip flushing for 36 hours, and it can't be faked, forgotten or unplugged. Japan's Zojirushi 'mimamori' kettle proved families will pay for a signal from an ordinary appliance. A utility meter is the same idea at the level of the whole house, and utilities are sitting on the data with no product.
first_30_days: Partner with two or three local home-care agencies and an Area Agency on Aging. Recruit 30 consenting seniors or families through caregiver support groups and Facebook groups for adult children. Install pulse or clamp-on readers on meters that support them, and run a 30-day baseline. Alert families by text and measure false-alarm and helpfulness rates. In parallel, approach one mid-size smart-meter utility with an opt-in pilot: consented data sharing at no cost, with the utility's logo on the program. Charge families $15 per month from day 31.

title: Age-Tier Compliance for Roblox-Style Creator Studios
one_liner: Pre-flight scanner and consulting that checks user-generated game experiences against Roblox Kids (<9), Select (9-15) and 16+ tier rules before discovery demotion costs revenue.
customer: UGC studios and creators earning $200k-$10M a year on Roblox and similar platforms (Fortnite UEFN), plus brand agencies commissioning sponsored experiences.
problem: Roblox mandated age checks (Jan 2026) and split into Kids, Select and standard tiers in June 2026. Experiences now must match a tier on chat, random-reward purchases, ads, voice and data collection. Misclassified experiences lose tier-based discovery. Indonesia's ban also covers Roblox. Studios don't understand how classification works and brand clients fear child-privacy liability.
solution: A 'tier lint' tool that combines public metadata with scripted play-throughs to flag features that clash with each tier, gives a fix list (for example, disable free text in Kids, replace loot boxes) and produces a 'brand-safe by tier' report for sponsors. A public changelog tracks platform policy changes.
why_now: The tier split is only three months old and the rules are still moving. Toy and media brands (Mattel's games push, per the brief) are commissioning kids' UGC experiences, and state attorney-general suits against Roblox (from memory) raise brand caution.
revenue_model: Subscription at $500-3k a month per studio, plus $5-15k audits for brand-sponsored experiences.
non_obvious_insight: Tiering turns content rating into distribution: the platform's discovery algorithm becomes the regulator, and the UGC studio, not Roblox, eats the cost of getting it wrong. That is a classic compliance-consultancy niche, like Amazon seller-policy work.
first_30_days: Scrape metadata on the top 500 experiences. Identify about 30 likely mis-tiered ones. Send each studio owner a personalized mini-audit. Sell 10 audits at $1.5k. Start a public policy-change newsletter to build trust.

title: Roll-Up of Compounding-Stranded Weight-Loss Clinics
one_liner: Buy distressed med spas and weight-loss clinics that lost their compounded GLP-1 margin, and convert them into aftercare-plus-aesthetics businesses.
customer: The clinics' patients, who pay memberships and procedures. Sellers are owners of weight-loss clinics, med spas and telehealth shells.
problem: FDA proposed excluding semaglutide, tirzepatide and liraglutide from the 503B bulks list on Apr 30, 2026 and sent ~55 warning letters to telehealth firms in Mar and Jun. Reportedly ~60% of med spas offered GLP-1 programs by 2025, many on compounded supply that peaked at ~30% of US volume. Owners want out, yet PE physician-practice deals are down ~50% in 2026, so buyers are scarce.
solution: Acquire 10-20 clinics at 0.3-0.8x revenue with seller notes and earn-outs. Convert to branded pill and vial cash programs, plus aftercare (muscle, nutrition, dose step-down), legal peptide offerings and aesthetics upsells. Centralize the medical director, billing and marketing.
why_now: The compounding cliff has stranded assets that are just patient relationships and licenses, while buyer capital retreated. 63% of 'Ozempic face' patients are cosmetic-clinic first-timers, so aesthetics cross-sell is real.
revenue_model: Clinic revenue of $199-399/month memberships plus procedures. Target ~25% EBITDA after integration, with a shared-services center.
non_obvious_insight: Distress plus absent buyers means near-free customer bases, and revenue per patient can rise after the switch to branded drugs plus aftercare. Earn-outs limit downside if patients churn.
first_30_days: Pull state med-spa and pharmacy lists and Instagram GLP-1 advertisers. Contact 100 owners, sign 2 LOIs with seller notes, and close the first acquisition of $150-300k with an integration playbook.

title: Universal Depot Operator for Stacked EPR Programs
one_liner: One neutral drop-off depot per town that serves batteries, paint, oil containers, textiles and small e-waste for many producer responsibility programs at once.
customer: PROs and stewardship programs (Circular Action Alliance, battery, paint and other stewardship organizations) under a master service agreement, plus host sites paid a host fee.
problem: EPR programs multiply, each building its own thin collection network. Colorado's Interchange 360 (petroleum containers) diverted about 2,500 lb in six months across 10 collection facilities, roughly 250 lb per site. Unit costs per pound are absurd, host sites drown in per-program rules, and households face a different trip per program.
solution: A shared depot at transfer stations and hardware stores with one trained staff, fire-safe cabinets and one weekly consolidated pickup. It is operated under a multi-PRO contract paid per pound plus a site fee. It starts in Colorado and Oregon and adds streams as new programs launch (California's SB 501 medium-format batteries, textiles).
why_now: Colorado's programs are just moving from planning to practice. Oregon's EPR survived the Commerce Clause challenge (Aug 2026) even as NAW appeals, and CAA collected $145.5M in 2025 while spending $56.5M, so budget exists to solve collection cost.
revenue_model: Per-lb handling fees and per-site fees from multiple PROs, host-fee share, and minor resale of recovered commodities.
non_obvious_insight: EPR is designed by material stream but households experience it by trip. The missing layer is a neutral aggregator that turns N programs into one drop-off and one truck.
first_30_days: Meet PRO operations leads in Colorado and Oregon. Pick 3 host sites in one county (a transfer station and 2 hardware stores). Price cabinets and a pickup route. Sign one PRO pilot on cost-plus terms.

title: Craft Data: Retiring Machinists Teach Robots
one_liner: Pay shops to let experienced craftspeople wear cameras and gloves, and sell the captured factory-floor skill data to robot-learning labs.
customer: Robot foundation-model and humanoid companies buying training data. Shops are the second customer, receiving cash and auto-generated standard work instructions.
problem: Physical AI funding hit $18.6B in Q2 2026, but labs lack high-quality real-world industrial manipulation data (setups, fixturing, deburring, measuring by feel). Meanwhile a retiring workforce takes unrecorded tacit skill, and no dataset of it exists.
solution: An egocentric capture kit (head and wrist cameras, instrumented glove, audio narration) worn during normal work. Add job context from CAM programs and travelers. Deliver curated, annotated datasets to labs. Shops receive setup videos, SOPs and a training library, and workers share in revenue, with consent, IP and safety protocols agreed up front.
why_now: Record physical-AI funding, cheap wearable capture hardware, imitation-learning advances, and a retirement wave. Labs need real industrial data, not lab data.
revenue_model: Target $150-400 per curated hour from labs (to validate with first buyers). Pay shops about $40 an hour. $500 a month per shop for the SOP and training library.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce input to robot learning is expertise, not compute. The same footage is a shop's best defense against retirement knowledge loss, so shops will host the capture and even pay for the by-product.
first_30_days: Recruit five shops with free SOP videos as the hook. Capture 100 hours. Pitch five labs with samples. Aim for one paid pilot of $20-50k. Hire an employment lawyer for consent and IP terms.

title: Deposit Gate That Kills Korean Bulk-Order Scams
one_liner: A KakaoTalk-native verify-and-deposit link that small Korean restaurants, bakeries and caterers send to any big or suspicious order, since scammers never pay a deposit and real customers do.
customer: Korean self-employed food, bakery, flower and catering owners who take phone or chat bulk orders. They pay ₩9,900/month plus a 1.5-2.5% take rate on deposits. Restaurant and bakery associations, POS vendors and card acquirers are distribution partners.
problem: The 'no-show scam' impersonates a government office, military unit, broadcaster or political party and places a large legitimate-looking order. The scammer then asks the owner to buy unrelated goods from a designated supplier, promising to pay for everything together. The owner pays the fake supplier and loses the money. It is 100% preventable by process, yet owners are alone on the phone and busy.
solution: The owner taps a Kakao chatbot or shortcut during the call. The caller receives a verify-and-deposit link: PASS phone identity, a claimed-organization check against official directories with call-back numbers, and a 10-30% deposit via KakaoPay or Toss. A tripwire flags any request to buy from a third-party supplier, which is the hallmark of stage two of the scheme. Scams die at the deposit step. Legitimate bulk buyers pay a small deposit, which also cuts ordinary no-shows.
why_now: H1 2025 losses were roughly 90% of the whole of 2024, with per-case damage up more than 50% year on year. Scammers keep widening the impersonations to entertainment agencies, broadcasters and political parties. Authorities' advice is already 'ask for a deposit', but nothing operationalizes it for a shop owner. KakaoPay and Toss make micro-deposit links trivial.
revenue_model: ₩9,900/month per shop, plus 1.5-2.5% of each deposit processed. B2B2C licensing to POS and reservation vendors, and fraud-loss underwriting data for card and insurance partners.
non_obvious_insight: The theft is not the food order, it is the redirected procurement in stage two, so a single rule ('never buy from a supplier the customer names') is nearly precision-perfect and a deposit is a perfect filter. Police-reported H1 2025 damage was ₩115.5 billion (1,155억 won) across 3,936 cases, about ₩29M per case (https://www.straightnews.co.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=311867 and https://www.ccmessage.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=121353). The two-stage method and the government's own advice to require deposits and reject out-of-scope purchases are described at https://www.viva100.com/article/20250623501489. The same article cites a Hyundai Research Institute estimate that ordinary no-shows cost hospitality ₩4.5 trillion a year, so the scam-defense wedge extends into a much larger deposit-booking market.
first_30_days: Days 1-7: Build a Kakao Channel bot that sends a hosted page with PASS auth, a deposit request via a payment gateway such as Toss Payments, and a scam-pattern checklist. Days 8-20: Offer free pilots to 50 shops via bakery, catering and restaurant owner Kakao open-chat groups and the local Food Service Association branch, with a scam-script sticker for the phone. Days 21-30: Convert the pilots that actually used it, publish a first 'blocked scam' tally, and approach one POS vendor and one card-acquirer with a co-branded offer.

title: Booth-Day Cover: Weather-Out Insurance for Vendors
one_liner: A $5-$15 add-on at booth-application checkout that pays vendors their booth fee plus a loss tier when rain, wind, heat or smoky air wrecks an outdoor event day.
customer: Art-fair exhibitors, farmers' market growers, food-truck and craft-fair vendors, sold at checkout through event organizers and vendor-booking platforms.
problem: Vendors prepay $150-$900 in booth fees plus travel and perishable inventory. When an event is rained out, wind-cancelled, or smoke keeps customers home, organizers rarely refund, and event-cancellation insurance protects only the organizer. The vendor is the uninsured party, and smoke-driven closures are increasingly common.
solution: Per-booth-day parametric micro-policies triggered by hourly station and radar data (rain over a threshold during market hours, gusts above a limit, heat index/WBGT, AirNow/PurpleAir AQI at or above 151). Payout tiers of $75-$500 are set by booth fee. Cover is sold via API in the booking checkout. Organizers get a 'weather-safe vendors' badge, a revenue share and a dashboard. Claims are automatic and paid to the vendor's payout account.
why_now: Smoke seasons since 2023 made AQI-linked outdoor closures routine. Hyperlocal sensor networks and 1 km radar rainfall data are cheap. Embedded-insurance APIs make per-transaction cover easy to bolt onto checkouts. A likely very strong El Niño (CPC/IRI, September 2026) points to a wet winter in the southern tier, where winter markets and festival seasons run.
revenue_model: Premium of about $6-$12 per booth-day at a 20-30% loading over expected loss, with 15-20% shared with the organizer or platform. Later, multi-event season passes and organizer-side cancellation cover.
non_obvious_insight: In outdoor events the vendor is the uninsured party, and a booth-day is a near-perfect unit of insurance: known date, place, price and trigger. The checkout is the underwriting file and weather data is the claims adjuster, so there is almost no claims cost.
first_30_days: Pitch two or three regional market associations and one art-fair or festival platform. Underwrite through a parametric MGA. Ship a Stripe checkout link with a simple rain/AQI/wind trigger table. Pilot 100 vendors at about $6 each across fall festival season and publish the first payout story.

title: Opt-Out Time Machine for AI Training Compliance
one_liner: A historical archive of every site's machine-readable AI-training opt-outs (robots.txt, TDMRep, ai.txt, meta tags, headers) so model builders can prove what was reserved on the day they crawled.
customer: AI startups and labs that train or fine-tune on scraped or third-party data (especially EU-exposed), dataset publishers, and rights-holder groups (publishers, collecting societies) that need proof of their own reservations.
problem: GPAI obligations have applied since Aug 2025 and AI Office enforcement began in Aug 2026. Providers need a copyright policy and must respect machine-readable rights reservations under the EU text-and-data-mining exception (background, verify). Opt-out signals change over time and nobody retains neutral evidence of what a site said on a given day, yet disputes will turn on exactly that.
solution: A weekly crawl of the top ~50M domains capturing robots.txt, /.well-known/tdmrep.json, ai.txt, meta tags, headers and terms-page hashes, stored as signed, timestamped snapshots. API calls answer 'what did domain X reserve at time T?' and 'filter dataset D by reservations as of T'. Certificates of compliance for training corpora and monitoring alerts for rights holders whose reservations are ignored.
why_now: Enforcement powers over GPAI providers began Aug 2026, copyright-and-training cases are moving through European courts, and crawl and storage costs are low enough for a two-person team.
revenue_model: API subscriptions of $2-25k/month for labs and dataset teams, $5-30k per compliance certificate, and $500-5k/month for rights-holder monitoring.
non_obvious_insight: Compliance evidence is a time-series problem. The neutral party that started archiving earlier owns the truth, and it cannot be recreated retroactively, so the moat begins accumulating on day one.
first_30_days: Crawl the top 1M domains weekly (a few hundred dollars a month) and publish a free opt-out prevalence report. Sign three EU AI startups or dataset publishers to paid pilots of $2-5k and approach one collecting society.

title: Independent Referee for Survey Panel Data
one_liner: An audit that tells research buyers what share of their online-panel responses came from bots, agents or fraud farms, and recalibrates the study against a verified-human control sample.
customer: Insights heads at CPG, pharma and financial-services firms, UX-research teams, academic labs and pollsters who buy panel sample from third-party vendors at $5-500 per complete.
problem: One prompt to a commercial AI agent now passes screeners and attention checks. A controlled evaluation found synthetic respondents passing 99.8% of 6,000 attention-check trials. As little as 3-7% contaminated responses can invalidate conclusions. Panel vendors both sell the sample and score its quality, so buyers cannot trust the referee.
solution: A per-study data-quality audit. Response files (timings, paradata, device data, open-ends) go through a detection ensemble plus honeypot items. A subset of the same questionnaire goes to a small address-recruited, device-attested human panel as a ground-truth control. Deliver an audit stamp, contamination-adjusted estimates, and a vendor scorecard across suppliers.
why_now: Survey-fraud research in 2025-26 shows agents beating attention checks. An MIT-run $50K challenge is testing detection, and NORC published a fraud literature review. Election-season polling and pharma sample budgets raise the stakes, and buyers are asking who audits the panels.
revenue_model: $3-15k per study audit, $50-150k per year programmes for insights teams that spend $2-10M on sample, and vendor-scorecard subscriptions.
non_obvious_insight: Most anti-fraud tooling is sold by panel sellers, whose incentive is to under-report fraud. The scarce asset is not detection code but an independent, verified-human comparison group, because you cannot prove what is fake without a known-real reference.
first_30_days: Recruit about 2,000 verified humans by address-based mail or a university survey-centre partnership. Buy sample from six panel vendors yourself and publish a 'state of sample quality' benchmark. Offer free audits to five insights leaders who have posted about bad data.

title: Reserve-Crew Backup Photographers for Wedding Day Emergencies
one_liner: A paid-standby bench of pre-vetted, style-matched backup photographers who can be dispatched within 2-3 hours, sold to solo photographers as a subscription and to wedding insurers as claims fulfillment.
customer: Solo and small-studio wedding photographers ($199-399/yr for a 'Continuity Guarantee' they can promise couples), plus wedding-insurance carriers and MGAs that cover vendor failure but cannot produce a person.
problem: Every solo photographer's nightmare is a sudden illness, crash or family emergency six hours before a wedding. The standard backup plan in contracts is 'a photographer friend', which fails in practice. On peak Saturdays (dates like 10/10/26) every competent local shooter is already booked, so the Facebook SOS post at 6am gets 40 sympathetic comments and zero style-matched, available humans. Whoever does show up has never seen the timeline, venue notes, family-formals list or the photographer's look. Wedding insurance reimburses money after the fact but cannot supply a competent human in three hours. It is a capacity-reservation problem, not an insurance problem.
solution: Members upload style samples plus a 'Continuity Pack' for each booked wedding (timeline, family list, venue and light notes, gallery drop link), all in one place. We maintain a regional bench of vetted shooters tagged by style (documentary, bright and airy, moody, film-look). Bench shooters are paid a small standby retainer (about $40) to hold peak dates, plus an activation fee ($500-900) paid by the member or the insurer. On activation, the pack is pushed to the understudy, a coordinator handles couple communication, and images are delivered under the member's brand. Members display a 'Continuity Guaranteed' badge, which becomes a booking-conversion asset.
why_now: Vendor-failure cover is now a standard add-on in wedding insurance, and 2026 contracts increasingly require a comparable replacement or a full refund, so the gap between reimbursing money and supplying a photographer is now visible and contractual. Weekend supply is squeezed onto peak dates, and a growing pool of freelance portrait, real-estate and second-shooter talent with open weekends can be organized cheaply through Stripe Connect and shared workspaces. Insurers are also under pressure to reduce claim severity in small commercial lines.
revenue_model: $99-399/yr member subscription (tiered by number of weddings), per-activation fee split with the bench shooter (we keep about 20%), and an insurer contract of a flat per-policy fee or per-claim fulfillment fee. Standby retainers are funded from the subscription pool, like airline reserve crews.
non_obvious_insight: Backup fails precisely on the dates it is needed, because scarcity is correlated. The free 'photographer friend' network evaporates on peak Saturdays. The only fix is paying for reserved capacity in advance, and once you do, you own the only reliable answer to the industry's most feared event.
first_30_days: Pick one metro. Sign 25 solo photographers as founding members at $99/yr and recruit 8 bench shooters (portrait, real-estate and second-shooter talent with open Saturdays). Build the Continuity Pack in Notion/Airtable plus a shared Google Drive. Run a fire drill: on a chosen Saturday, ping every member's pack and time how fast each is delivered to a bench shooter. Pitch two wedding-insurance MGAs on a 90-day claims-fulfillment pilot, and get a lawyer to check contractor and liability terms before the first live activation.

title: Archival Footage Authenticity Clearance for Documentaries
one_liner: A per-film clearance service that proves each archival still and clip is real, so producers and E&O insurers can sign off.
customer: Independent documentary producers, YouTube documentary channels and news video teams, plus clearance consultants and E&O brokers that refer them.
problem: Clearance houses check rights, not reality. Stock libraries and search results now contain AI-made 'archival' images, and one fake in a true-crime doc becomes a public scandal, as with the AI images alleged in Netflix's What Jennifer Did (2024). E&O underwriters ask for clearance procedures. Visible AI watermarks are unreliable, since removers for Sora output appeared within a week of its launch.
solution: Fixed-price audit of a film's cut list. For each asset: trace it to the earliest source via reverse search and archive catalogs, run metadata and codec forensics, check C2PA and SynthID where available, run a detector ensemble, and produce a provenance chain. Deliver a per-asset source dossier and a producer's memo formatted for insurers and distributors. A portal re-checks only assets that change between cuts.
why_now: Sora's shutdown (app Apr 26, API Sep 24) removes one source, but open video models keep flooding stock sources. Streamers publish AI guidelines, and TikTok's C2PA membership in Jul 2026 normalizes provenance checks.
revenue_model: $1.5-10k per film, $500-3k/month for YouTube documentary or news teams, and referral fees from clearance consultants.
non_obvious_insight: Rights clearance is already a budgeted line item in every documentary. Authenticity clearance is a new column in an existing spreadsheet, so it does not need a new budget line.
first_30_days: Reach five documentary producers via the International Documentary Association and doc-maker Slack groups. Run a free audit on one recently published film's archival section, partner with two clearance consultants for referrals, and charge $2.5k for the next five.

title: Robot Pack-Opening with Chain-of-Custody
one_liner: A neutral facility and machine that opens sealed trading-card packs on camera without human hands, sorts hits and ships them, so buyers can trust a break.
customer: Live-stream breakers and repack sellers, game stores running mail-in breaks, and buyers who pay for the 'bot-opened' badge.
problem: Fraud in streamed breaks includes resealed packs with hits removed, counterfeits and non-delivery. Whatnot did about $8B in 2025 and is under litigation, X-ray pack scanning is sold to collectors, and breakers spend heavy labor opening thousands of packs.
solution: A semi-automated cell (slitter, camera, card ID, sleeving) with serial-logged tamper-evident intake seals, a public feed with an audit trail, and a badge. Start as a neutral facility with humans in the loop, opening product breakers ship in, then lease the machine to large breakers.
why_now: Vision-language robot control matured in 2025-26. Litigation and fraud make trust monetizable, and the 2026 robbery wave favors a secured central facility over home streaming setups.
revenue_model: $0.40-1.00 per pack opened, per-hit shipping fees, badge subscriptions and machine leasing.
non_obvious_insight: Trust in breaks is a chain-of-custody problem, not a reputation problem. A machine has no motive to skim hits. Labor arbitrage pays for the machine while trust earns the price premium.
first_30_days: Rent a small secure space and run hands-off, sealed-bag-intake openings for 5 breakers with two part-timers and a phone rig. Charge per pack and prototype the cutter with an off-the-shelf arm.

title: Supplier-side questionnaire firewall citing the VSME cap
one_liner: A forward-to tool that answers big customers' ESG, NIS2 and EUDR questionnaires from one evidence vault and flags which questions the law says a small supplier can decline.
customer: EU SMEs and small mid-caps (under 1,000 staff) that supply larger companies, bought through accountants, tax advisors and chambers of commerce who add it as a service to their clients.
problem: Since Omnibus I took effect on 18 March 2026, CSRD-scope buyers cannot require value-chain partners with 1,000 or fewer employees to provide more sustainability information than the voluntary SME standard (VSME) sets out. The VSME basic module covers business description, workforce, energy and Scope 1 and 2 emissions. The cap does not cover NIS2 security questionnaires, EUDR data, voluntary customer targets or bid competition. Suppliers still get differently formatted questionnaires from every customer and lender, and most cannot tell which asks are legally capped.
solution: Suppliers forward each customer questionnaire (Excel, PDF or portal export) to an inbox. The tool parses it and maps each question to a canonical evidence vault: VSME basic answers, energy and payroll-derived Scope 1 and 2 numbers, a NIS2-lite control evidence set, and a supplier code of conduct. It auto-drafts answers. It also classifies every question as 'inside the cap', 'outside the cap, with a cited polite decline paragraph', or 'not covered by the cap (NIS2, EUDR, voluntary)'. The vault is built by pulling data the accountant already holds. Accountants get a multi-client dashboard.
why_now: The cap is 6 months old and the VSME Delegated Act was published in July 2026, so customers' procurement teams are still sending old-format questionnaires. Germany's NIS2 law took effect on 6 Dec 2025 and BSI says regulated entities will grow from about 4,500 to about 29,500, which multiplies supplier security questionnaires. CSDDD also limits information requests to smaller firms, but application is not until 2029.
revenue_model: White-label to accountancies at EUR 15-30 per client per month, or direct at EUR 49-99 per month per SME. Add EUR 150-300 for a one-off 'initial vault build' for firms not served by an accountant.
non_obvious_insight: The crowded market sells to large buyers who send questionnaires. The legally new wedge is the supplier's right to refuse, plus the accountant, who already holds energy and payroll data and is trusted. Evidence: after 18 March 2026 large CSRD companies 'cannot require value-chain partners with 1,000 or fewer employees to provide more sustainability information than ... VSME', but the same source warns that 'Nothing stops a buyer choosing the bidder who turned up with clean, current numbers' and that Scope 1 and 2 are non-negotiable, so suppliers need both a decline lever and a ready pack (https://www.dashe.ai/blog/big-customer-asked-for-your-emissions/). Suppliers to NIS2 entities 'should expect questionnaires' and sending a 300-question form is common (https://www.3rdrisk.com/blog/seven-nis2-questions-to-ask). Germany's NIS2 registration had only 38.5% compliance by the March 2026 deadline (https://www.cloudmagazin.com/en/2026/03/22/nis2-and-saas-supply-chain-compliance-gap/).
first_30_days: Collect 30 real questionnaires by offering accountants a free 'questionnaire triage' in exchange for the redacted files. Hand-map them to a 60-row canonical answer sheet. Build the classify-and-decline prototype on that set. Pitch 5 small accounting firms and 2 chamber-of-commerce sustainability desks with a live demo on a client's own questionnaire. Aim for 3 paying accountancy pilots.

title: Friday Programs for Four-Day School Districts
one_liner: A turnkey 'fifth-day' care and enrichment operator that runs in existing school buildings for districts on four-day weeks, funded by parent fees and vouchers.
customer: Rural and small-town districts on four-day weeks (hundreds of districts across 20+ states, from memory) and their working parents. Also 21st CCLC and state after-school grant programs.
problem: Districts adopted four-day weeks to cut costs and recruit teachers. The off day leaves working parents with no care in places where licensed slots are already scarce, so kids stay alone, with grandparents or parents leave jobs. Each district improvises its own Friday program.
solution: An operating kit: a staffing pool (education majors and retired teachers), background-check pipeline, daily curriculum, parent sign-up and payment, subsidy-voucher billing, insurance and transport. The district provides the building. We run the first sites ourselves, then license the kit for a management fee.
why_now: ESSER money ended, so more districts are trimming days (from memory). Childcare prices are up 29% since 2020 and rural supply is thin. CCDF rules moving to enrollment-based payment help small operators get paid reliably.
revenue_model: Parent fee of $35-50 per child per day, with a 15% management fee or per-site licence when franchised to local operators. Voucher billing adds funded slots.
non_obvious_insight: This desert is a day-of-week desert created by a policy choice, and the most expensive input (the building) is already paid for by taxpayers. That makes the unit economics better than standard childcare.
first_30_days: Call 20 four-day-week districts in Missouri, Oklahoma and Colorado. Run one paid pilot Friday with 15-25 kids at $40 a day. Recruit staff from the nearest college's education program. Track true margin per child-day and use the data to sell the second district.

title: Live-Action Fraud Drills Using Immersive Theater
one_liner: Ticketed and B2B immersive-theater experiences where participants, with consent, get scammed by actors and voice-cloned 'relatives' in a safe space and learn the tells under real emotional pressure.
customer: Credit unions, community banks and insurers that want measurable fraud-loss reduction among older customers; employers' security teams and finance, HR and IT-helpdesk staff (named targets of voice deepfakes); senior-living operators, libraries and AARP-style chapters. Escape-room and immersive-theater operators are licensees.
problem: Per the briefing, adults 60+ lost $7.7B in 2025 (up 59%), account for 66% of crypto-ATM losses, and law-enforcement-impersonation scams produced about 61,000 complaints and $1.6B+ with fake video calls. Conventional awareness training (videos, phishing simulations) shows little measurable effect; a 2025 study of about 19,500 UCSD Health employees found annual training had almost no impact on click rates (verify). Voice cloning now needs only 3 seconds of audio. The pressure tactics (urgency, secrecy, authority) are exactly what a lecture cannot simulate.
solution: A repeatable, franchisable 60-90 minute experience. Participants get a 'phone call' from an actor-controlled voice clone of a consenting volunteer (real-time voice conversion trained on the volunteer's own sample) or a fake CFO. They move through an escalating fraud script (fake bank, 'police', crypto-ATM instructions) with hidden facilitators, then a debrief teaches three tells and sets up a family or team safe-word protocol. Each participant leaves with a personalised safe-word card and help turning on their bank's trusted-contact feature. A B2B mobile 30-minute 'CFO voice-clone drill' scores the sponsor on how many people stop the transfer at each step. Outcomes are measured pre/post and at 90 days. Psychological-safety protocol and a counselor are built in.
why_now: October is Cybersecurity Awareness Month, when awareness budgets are spent. The FBI's 17 Sep 2026 PSA cites AI video calls in law-enforcement impersonation. Real-time voice conversion is cheap and voice-deepfake attacks are surging. Regulators are pushing banks to protect vulnerable customers (for example the UK's mandatory APP-fraud reimbursement since Oct 2024), so banks want provable prevention.
revenue_model: Sponsors pay $3-8k per community event of 30-60 participants, or $40-150 per employee for corporate drills. Licensing or franchise fees from venues (about $1.5k/month plus event share). Public ticketed shows at $25-40 with sponsor underwriting.
non_obvious_insight: Fraud victims are not ignorant. They are overwhelmed by staged emotion under time pressure, and skills learned in calm classrooms fail under stress. Live-experience designers know how to induce and safely release exactly that state, and security teams know the real scripts. Banks can also compute ROI in avoided losses, which theater companies cannot.
first_30_days: Pair an immersive-theater company with a fraud investigator. Prototype a 45-minute 'grandparent scam' and a 'CFO deepfake' scenario with consent forms and a licensed counselor. Pilot with two credit unions and one library during October at about $2.5k each. Measure pre/post behavior with a follow-up test call. Use results to sell to regional credit-union leagues and security-awareness teams.

title: Leak-Proof Outsourcing Passport for Game Studios
one_liner: Contractor identity checks at first build access, per-recipient build watermarking and reusable vendor security attestations for the outsourcing chain (art, audio, QA, porting) that leaks unreleased games.
customer: Mid-size and AA/indie publishers that outsource to 20-200 external vendors. Also the vendors themselves (art studios in Poland, Vietnam, India and elsewhere, QA houses, localization and voice studios, freelance marketplaces) who need a portable credential to win work.
problem: Layoffs and cost-cutting push more production to external vendors and freelancers. Per the briefing, Ubisoft headcount fell from 18,666 to 16,590 and EA's $55B buyout, which closed 4 Aug 2026, aims to cut operating costs by putting AI throughout. Each vendor has weaker security than the publisher while unreleased builds are the crown jewels (GTA VI launches 19 Nov 2026, and past leaks like Rockstar 2022, Insomniac 2023 and Game Freak 2024 show the pattern). Remote contractors are also prime targets for identity fraud: North Korean IT-worker schemes hit 'nearly 70' and 'over 100' US companies in cases sentenced in Apr-May 2026, using deepfake-assisted interviews and stolen identities. Film has the MPA's Trusted Partner Network; games have no equivalent.
solution: A subscription 'passport' with five parts. (1) Contractor identity verification with liveness and injection-attack detection at onboarding and again at first privileged build access, tied to device posture. (2) A game-specific vendor security attestation, evidence-based (SSO, endpoint, repo hygiene) and shared across publishers so a vendor is assessed once. (3) Per-recipient forensic watermarking of builds, assets and design documents so a leak can be traced to a person or vendor. (4) Offboarding automation for contract end or layoff waves. (5) Insurer-ready evidence packages for cyber and E&O cover.
why_now: EA's leveraged buyout, Ubisoft's restructuring and Tencent-backed Vantage carve-out are all driving outsourcing. GTA VI's launch date will attract extortion attempts. North Korean IT-worker cases and deepfake interview kits make hiring-time identity checks insufficient. The IDScan.net breach (153M license scans) makes zero-retention verification a selling point (per briefing), and enterprise identity products are crowded but none focus on game supply chains.
revenue_model: Publishers pay $1.5-6k/month plus $30-80 per contractor-month. Vendors pay $200-500/month for a portable attestation badge, giving vendor-pays adoption. Watermarking priced per build distribution.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is not the publisher's own security but that each publisher re-audits the same few hundred vendors. A shared 'assess once, reuse everywhere' passport (film's TPN model) is cheaper for publishers and turns vendors into paying customers. Identity must be verified at the moment of privileged access rather than at hiring, because proxy interviews and deepfakes defeat interview-time checks.
first_30_days: Partner with 2-3 mid-size publishers or a co-dev/QA outsourcer. Draft a 40-question game-specific assessment, wire up an existing IDV API plus a device-posture check, and pilot with one outsourcing vendor. Offer a 'leak-trace drill' using watermarks on a demo build. Sell to publishers' security leads at $1.5k/month pilots.

title: Ticket Escrow Bot for Fan Communities
one_liner: A payment-escrow bot for the Discord, WhatsApp and Facebook groups where fans already swap tickets, releasing money only when a cryptographically verifiable ticket-transfer email arrives.
customer: Fans aged 18-35 (K-pop, pop tours, esports, festivals, football supporters) trading tickets peer-to-peer, and the community admins and moderators who police scams manually. Fans pay the fee, and admins get a revenue share.
problem: Ticket fraud thrives in fan groups because the only 'proof' is a screenshot, and generative AI now forges tickets, receipts and transfer confirmations trivially. Official resale is distrusted: per the briefing, Oasis tickets went from GBP 135 to 350+ under dynamic pricing, StubHub's World Cup 2026 tickets failed to reach buyers with class actions following, and the UK CMA ordered StubHub to refund 50,000+ customers over drip pricing. Fans therefore keep swapping in groups, where scammers pretend to transfer tickets or sell the same ticket several times.
solution: The buyer pays into escrow. The seller performs the official transfer in the ticketing app (Ticketmaster, AXS, Eventim, Fever and similar). The buyer sends the platform's 'tickets received' email to a unique escrow address, either forwarded as an .eml attachment or through a narrowly scoped read-only mailbox filter for that sender only. The system validates the DKIM/ARC signature, sender domain, event, section and seat lines, and that the recipient is the buyer, then releases funds after a hold for barcode rotation. Extras: automatic enforcement of a group's face-value cap, light seller verification above thresholds, an admin-facing reputation ledger, and cancellation refunds through an insurance partner. Payments run through a licensed platform-payments partner rather than holding funds directly.
why_now: AI-forged screenshots have made image evidence worthless. Per the briefing, Live Nation lost a federal jury verdict on monopolization in April 2026 and resale fees are under fire, the FTC's all-in pricing rule took effect in May 2025, and StubHub's delivery failures have left fans without a trusted route. Ticketing platforms increasingly move tickets by wallet transfer, so signed transfer emails are now standard.
revenue_model: 4-6% fee on escrowed amount, split between buyer and seller, with 0.5-1% shared with community admins. Premium 'insured swap' add-on. B2B API for promoters that want a safe official fan-swap channel.
non_obvious_insight: You do not need to beat Ticketmaster or become a marketplace. Every major ticketing platform already emits a DKIM-signed transfer email that is very hard to fake, a cheap trust anchor no fan-group scammer can produce. The distribution channel is community admins, who already do unpaid trust-and-safety work and will adopt anything that reduces their scam reports.
first_30_days: Pick one fandom with a high-volume swap group (a K-pop tour or a football supporters' group). Run concierge escrow by hand with a payments-platform account and a script that checks .eml DKIM. Handle 100 swaps at 5% and publish 'scams avoided' stats. Onboard 10 admin partners with a revenue share. Check ticketing terms of service per market before scaling.

title: Purpose-Locked Guardian Funds for Pets
one_liner: A pre-funded account that pays a named pet guardian through a card locked to vet and pet spending when the owner dies or is hospitalized.
customer: Adults 55+ and single owners with dogs or cats, sold through estate-planning attorneys, hospice and palliative social workers, hospital discharge planners and senior-living communities. The named guardian is the user.
problem: When owners die, are hospitalized or enter care, pets often become shelter intakes. Pet trusts cost $1,500-3,000 in legal fees and rely on trust that money reaches the animal. An informal promise to a niece falls apart when she faces a $4,000 vet bill, and a dog's lifetime cost is about $34K. Pets are also a documented reason some older adults delay hospital care.
solution: A low-fee guardian account funded by lump sum, monthly premium or life-insurance beneficiary designation. On a verified trigger (death certificate, or a social worker's hospital admission attestation) the guardian receives a purpose-locked card restricted by merchant category to vet, food and boarding, plus a monthly stipend. A records vault carries vet history. A vetted foster network is the fallback if the guardian declines. Leftovers go to heirs or a named charity.
why_now: Card-issuing and BaaS APIs make purpose-restricted cards cheap. Vet costs have risen much faster than general prices, so guardianship is a real financial obligation. The large pandemic-era adoption cohort is aging, and more older adults live alone. Stablecoin-era interest in programmable, purpose-bound money has made restricted-use funds a familiar concept.
revenue_model: $149-199 setup fee, about 1.5% annual administration fee on balances, card interchange, and attorney or hospice referral fees. Insurers and employers may later fund it as a rider.
non_obvious_insight: The legal trust is not the product. The product is a guarantee that money reaches the animal and that a stranger can act fast, and purpose-locked spending is what delivers it. This is one of the few pet products where the buyer is not the beneficiary, so trust and distribution channels matter more than price.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 estate-planning attorneys and 3 hospice or palliative-care social-work teams in one metro. Sell a $149 'pet guardian plan' with a pooled trust via a licensed trust-company partner and a sponsor-bank card. Target 30 funded accounts of $1,000-3,000 each in the first quarter.

title: Cure Desk: Medical-Bill Triage for Delinquent Tenants
one_liner: A landlord-paid service that turns a late-rent notice into a medical-bill rescue, using hospital charity care, bill negotiation and coverage re-enrollment to free up the cash that pays the rent.
customer: Multifamily and single-family-rental operators (500-20,000 units) pay per cured account.
problem: 20% of renter households paid late or missed rent in 2025, and middle-income households jumped from 14.3% to 21.6%. About 4.8M people lost coverage after enhanced ACA subsidies expired. Landlords now face AI-assisted pro se tenant filings (41,000+ federal pro se cases in 2025) and increasingly conclude that cash-for-keys is cheaper than winning an eviction.
solution: When a resident is 3-5 days late, the property manager sends an opt-in text. If medical bills or a coverage loss are the cause, an advocate applies to the hospital's financial-assistance program (nonprofit hospitals must have one), negotiates the bill, sets payment plans and opens a special enrollment period. The landlord pays a success fee (roughly $300-500) only when arrears are cured, versus thousands per eviction.
why_now: Subsidy expiry created millions of self-pay patients in 2026, delinquency is at series highs, and the legal cost of eviction is rising with AI-generated filings. Medicaid churn from Jan 2027 will add more.
revenue_model: Success fee per cured account, with an optional $/unit/month retainer for early-warning outreach.
non_obvious_insight: A missed rent payment is the earliest and most reliable distress signal in consumer finance, and it lands on the one party with the data, scale and cash motive to pay someone to fix it. A tenant's hospital bill is far more negotiable than a landlord's arrears, so the fix comes from the health side.
first_30_days: Recruit two ex-hospital financial counselors. Sign two mid-size operators and run 200 delinquent accounts manually via SMS and a shared inbox. Track cure rate and cost per cure. Landlords pay only after cure.

title: Deorphanization Factory for AI-Nominated Enzymes
one_liner: A pooled-substrate, NGS-readout assay line that assigns function to hundreds of AI-nominated unknown enzymes per week for hundreds of dollars each.
customer: Genome-editing and enzyme-discovery companies, frontier-lab and academic agent-discovery teams, and industrial enzyme groups.
problem: Agent swarms nominate candidates far faster than anyone can characterize them. Anthropic's run went from 200,000+ reverse transcriptases to 20 candidates in 21 hours, yet the function of the resulting array-associated reverse transcriptase (ART) system is still unknown, with human validation and biochemical characterization as the bottleneck.
solution: Cell-free expression of candidates in 384-well format. Universal substrate panels of pooled, barcoded DNA and RNA oligo libraries are incubated with each enzyme. NGS reads out cutting, copying, ligating and editing, producing an automated activity 'passport' (substrate preferences, cofactors, temperature). Start with nucleic-acid-acting enzymes (nucleases, RTs, recombinases, ligases) where pooled NGS readout works, and add mass-spec panels for small-molecule enzymes later.
why_now: Anthropic's Sept 2026 ART discovery came with an explicit invitation to partner with other scientists. DNA synthesis is cheap, cell-free expression is mature, and agent discovery volumes are exploding.
revenue_model: $300-1,000 per enzyme passport, $50-250k discovery-partnership programs, and shared upside on licensed hits.
non_obvious_insight: Compute is commoditizing discovery, so the scarce step is cheap, standardized characterization. Pooled assays turn function into a read instead of a project. A passport format could become the exchange currency between agent discoverers and enzyme users.
first_30_days: Build a v0 pooled-substrate library and assay for reverse transcriptases and nucleases. Characterize 50 public candidates and publish the results. Approach 5 editing-tool companies and 3 academic agent-discovery groups with a $10k 50-enzyme pilot.

title: 72-Hour Diligence Engine for Vet Clinic Acquirers
one_liner: Upload a PIMS export and P&L and get retention cohorts, price-versus-volume decomposition and doctor-dependence risk in three days, then keep the same schema as the post-close KPI dashboard.
customer: Mid-size vet groups, search-fund and PE platforms buying 5-50 clinics a year, and practice lenders.
problem: Roll-ups are continuing (GoodVets buying WellHaven, 40+ hospitals), but small acquirers rely on broker packages and QuickBooks. PIMS exports differ by system, and price increases can hide falling active-client counts, a real risk given visits reportedly down three years.
solution: Ingest PIMS exports across major systems, normalize service lines, then compute cohort retention, active clients, revenue per DVM and tech utilization, price/mix/volume decomposition, discount and controlled-substance anomalies, and revenue at risk if the owner-vet leaves. Output a quality-of-earnings-lite memo, then continue as a post-merger KPI dashboard.
why_now: M&A pace is high, buyers include newer and smaller platforms without in-house analytics, and LLMs make messy export mapping cheap. Incumbents such as IDEXX are buying workflow AI (CoVet), not diligence tooling.
revenue_model: $3-6K per target for diligence, $1-2K per clinic per month for post-close dashboards.
non_obvious_insight: The price hikes that flatter EBITDA may be masking client attrition. Diligence that sees through price versus volume is worth far more than its fee, and brokers will not build it because it works against their headline numbers.
first_30_days: Approach 10 mid-size groups and search funds with a free retrospective on one closed deal. Build export mappers for 3 major PIMS. Sell 3 paid diligences at $3K each.

title: Junior Studio OS for Teen Game Developers
one_liner: Payroll, enforceable contracts, a custodial legal shell and payout splitting for teenage Roblox and Fortnite creator teams that already run large studios without knowing they are businesses.
customer: Teen (13-19) founders of UGC game studios and their parents, plus adult publishers, investors and acquirers who want to back teen studios safely.
problem: Roblox creators earned over $1.5B in 2025, and top studios are run by teens and early twenties. But minors can disaffirm contracts, collaborators across countries expect revenue splits, payouts land in personal or parent accounts, taxes are misunderstood, and there is no cap table. Disputes and co-founders who leave with the IP kill studios, and investors avoid them.
solution: A 'studio in a box': a custodial LLC or UTMA structure with guardian co-signature and court-approval flow for larger deals. A rev-share ledger reads DevEx and group payouts and splits them automatically. It collects W-9/W-8 forms and sets aside tax reserves. It provides a parent-co-signed, ratify-at-18 contract template with IP assignment and vesting, plus a diligence data room for acquirers.
why_now: Roblox creator payouts were over $1.5B in 2025 (about 70% year-over-year growth), the standard DevEx rate rose to $0.0038 per Robux in September 2025, and 2026 rate changes reward higher-spending audiences. Teen studios are hiring peers and getting publisher attention. Fortnite (UEFN) and Minecraft marketplaces add more teen earners.
revenue_model: SaaS of $19-$49 per month per studio plus 1-2% on managed payouts, a $500-$2,500 legal setup package, and diligence or introduction fees from publishers and investors.
non_obvious_insight: Their barrier is not creativity, it is legal personhood. When a 15-year-old's game earns $20k per month, the biggest risk is a co-founder who quits with the IP or a signature that is not binding. Selling enforceable trust wins the studio and later the deal flow, making the OS the accepted source of diligence on teen studios.
first_30_days: Join the top 50 Roblox developer Discords and the DevForum. Offer a free 'who owns what' studio audit to 30 teen studios. Sell a $299 done-for-you custodial entity plus rev-share agreement drafted by a youth-entertainment lawyer, and get 10 paying by day 30. Pitch three UGC publishers on sourcing through you.

title: Outage Pucks: Street-Level Blackout Cover
one_liner: A $25 plug-in sensor that proves your power is out and triggers a cash payout after 12 dark hours, turning neighborhoods of pucks into their own insurance oracle and a data feed utilities will pay for.
customer: Small food businesses (corner stores, taquerias, bakeries, daycares, ghost kitchens) and households with power-dependent medical needs (home oxygen, CPAP, insulin fridges, breast-milk storage). Secondary buyers are utilities and municipal resilience programs.
problem: Outage losses (spoiled inventory, closed days, hotel stays) are small and frequent, and today they are effectively uninsurable. Utility tariffs limit liability, homeowners policies mostly ignore off-premises power failure, and no address-level proof of an outage exists, so no product can pay automatically.
solution: A cellular, battery-backed puck reports loss of mains power with tamper detection. Outages are confirmed by cross-verification when several pucks on the same feeder or block go dark together, plus utility outage feeds. Payouts are $100 at 12 hours and $100 per additional 12 hours up to $600, with a higher medical tier. The anonymized street-level outage map is sold to utilities, regulators and insurers.
why_now: Grid stress from aging distribution lines, surging data-center load and public safety power shutoffs in the West is a live concern for households and small businesses. LTE-M hardware is cheap and instant-payout rails exist. CPC/IRI's September 2026 outlooks show a very strong El Niño likely, which means an active southern storm track over California and the Gulf and Southeast this winter.
revenue_model: Puck-plus-cover subscription of $8-$12 per month, with premium share to the carrier/MGA. Data licensing to utilities and grid-resilience programs, and grant or utility-funded seats for medical-baseline customers.
non_obvious_insight: Crowd verification lets a device fleet act as a parametric oracle at a resolution utilities themselves lack on low-voltage segments, where they often learn of outages only when customers call. The insurance product pays for the sensor network, and the sensor network is the real asset.
first_30_days: Buy 200 off-the-shelf LTE-M power-loss sensors and firmware-tag them. Place them with a restaurant association and a home-health agency in one storm or shutoff-prone metro. Launch as a capped 'outage guarantee' service warranty from the company's own balance sheet while an MGA is lined up. Pitch the aggregated outage map to one utility resilience team.
